text: WSJ: Mexico's Press Is Still Free Under Sheinbaum August 19, 2026 | 🟢 📰 The WSJ ran Mary O'Grady's "Sheinbaum Moves to Gag Mexico's Media" — then printed the government's reply on the same opinion page. Foreign Secretary Roberto Velasco: Mexico's press "is not silenced." 🔍 Worth noting when it happens: the outlet that swung gave the target space to answer with evidence. • "It is not a matter of rhetoric. It is a matter of evidence, and the facts contradict her claim." • Velasco: Mexico is living "the freest and most democratic moment in its history." Source

🇲🇽📈 <u>THE PESO BROKE BELOW 17 TO THE DOLLAR</u>

The peso closed Thursday at 16.9573 per dollar, its strongest level since 2024, and is up 5.8 percent against the dollar so far in 2026, El Financiero reports. Sheinbaum credited a "very solid economy" and international confidence: "If there were no international confidence in the Mexican economy, the peso would not be where it is." The strength cuts both ways, importers and firms carrying dollar debt gain, while remittance recipients, tourism and oil revenue lose ground.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>US COURT THROWS OUT WASHINGTON'S ORDER TO BREAK UP AEROMÉXICO-DELTA</u>

A US appeals court struck down the Department of Transportation's move to dissolve the Aeroméxico-Delta joint venture, calling the demand disproportionate and arbitrary and restoring the antitrust immunity the airlines had been granted. DOT had branded the alliance "legalized collusion" and pointed to the roughly 60 percent of cross-border flights the two carriers control, but the airlines showed Washington applied stricter standards to them than to comparable joint ventures in Asia. Schedules, fares and capacity stay coordinated.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>ARREST OF CUÉN'S EX-DRIVER REOPENS THE MAYO ZAMBADA FILE</u>

Mexico's FGR has arrested Fausto Corrales, former driver for ex-UAS rector Héctor Melesio Cuén, and Sheinbaum called the arrest "relevant" to clarifying what happened on 25 July 2024, the day Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada was taken against his will to the United States. Prosecutors identify Corrales as the man who drove Cuén to the ranch in Huertos del Pedregal, Culiacán, where that meeting allegedly took place. A Mexican citizen was removed from Mexican soil by force, and the case is still open here.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SIX JUSTICES VOTED THEMSELVES BACK PRIVATE MEDICAL INSURANCE</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court restored publicly funded major medical insurance for judicial staff, on an initiative from Justice Yasmín Esquivel and five colleagues. Sheinbaum's reply from the National Palace: "Something happens when they walk into that building. They get transformed. It must be haunted by the spirits of the past." She called Benito Juárez "the best president the Court has ever had" and reminded them he spent his life fighting fueros and privilege. Public servants have ISSSTE and IMSS Bienestar. "If they want to pay for private insurance out of their own salary, go ahead."

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX HAS PAID 95% OF ITS OVERDUE SUPPLIER DEBT</u>

Roughly 95 percent of the Pemex suppliers and service providers who were owed late payments have now been paid, President Sheinbaum said at Thursday's morning press conference. "I don't dare give a percentage, but it is close to 95 percent of the suppliers whose payments had fallen behind." She acknowledged a few cases remain, some dating back to 2024, including small business owners who raised it with her during her visit to Tamaulipas last weekend.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO BLOCKED 37 FUEL-SMUGGLING OPERATIONS IN 17 MONTHS</u>

Since March 2025 Mexican authorities have stopped 37 attempts to bring contraband fuel into the country, seizing more than 12.4 million liters and hitting the networks for 318 million pesos, according to security cabinet documents. Thirteen of those attempts came through the ports of Altamira and Coatzacoalcos. The mapped network starts with two suppliers sharing one Houston address, Ikon Midstream and Hevi Transport, moves through an importer declaring the fuel as "additives," and ends at Azteca Cone, a ghost firm that also served the CJNG.
